public.problem: You teach the same students every week, but your booking page makes you schedule each lesson one at a time. A 12-week term for 40 students means hundreds of bookings, and you lose an evening every month doing it. When a lesson moves, you only find out from an old email.

ideas.problemStatement: "I'm literally scheduling 700+ meetings one by one" each term for 50+ students; coaches book 16-week series by hand; one practitioner rebooks 80 to 120 fixed appointments a month, "6 to 7 hours every month", hitting CAPTCHAs after about 10 bookings an hour, while competitors "have had this feature for years".
ideas.description: The teacher connects Calendly and creates one hidden 'series' event type with an unlimited date range. For each student they choose a weekday, time and number of weeks; the app generates the dates, skips the teacher's holidays and blocked days, checks each date against Calendly's open slots, and books them through Calendly's Create Event Invitee API, so Calendly's own confirmations, calendar invites and workflows run as normal. Large terms are queued across days to stay inside Calendly's limits, and the teacher sees honest progress. Webhooks keep a per-student log of reschedules and cancellations, and the student gets one email listing every date.
ideas.targetCustomer: Self-employed music teachers, tutors and coaches on paid Calendly plans who book recurring sessions for 10 to 40 students on their behalf.
ideas.buyer: The teacher or coach, on a personal or business card, alongside the Calendly subscription they already pay for.
ideas.whyNow: Calendly opened its Scheduling API (Create Event Invitee) and webhooks to every plan on 2026-11-03, so a small app can book on a teacher's behalf for the first time without an Enterprise deal; meanwhile recurring-booking complaints on Calendly's community ran from August to November 2026 with no native feature shipped.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan can build the recurrence and conflict engine and the queue on the HintWise platform alone, and the buyers are teachers: tutoring and lesson businesses are a market he understands from education, without depending on his own students.

scoreRationale.feasibility: Create Event Invitee and webhooks are open on all plans (https://developer.calendly.com/release-notes/2026/11/3), but the 100-a-day cap and open-slot rule need a queue (https://developer.calendly.com/api-docs/overview/rate-limits.md).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Email and scheduling data only; Calendly sends the texts (https://developer.calendly.com/api-docs/calendly-api/scheduled-events/create-event-invitee.md).

review.findings: Reviewer re-read 6165 and 5679 and fetched Calendly's November 2026 release notes, the MCP tool list, Callie help pages, cal.com and calendly.com pricing. No add-on, extension, Zapier template or GitHub project books a series inside Calendly; the Zapier route makes a Google Calendar event and loses Calendly reminders. Callie is beta on premium plans and books single meetings; the hosted MCP server lets technical users loop single bookings. Cal.com's free plan has no recurring events (Teams $12). Calendly staff are researching the gap (6135). Poster A's two threads count once; poster F (May) is outside 90 days; one poster already left for Acuity. Feasibility cut from 4 to 3: 5 API bookings a day on Free, 100 on paid plans, open-slot rule during multi-day queues, paid event types blocked, text-reminder consent for API bookings untested. Re-scoped to paid-Calendly teachers with 10 to 40 students, a hidden series event type, and an honest queue. Total 20 to 19.

ideas.summary: For small US firms on QuickBooks Online: send invoices and payment reminders from your own email domain, with a record of exactly what each client received.

public.summary: Send your invoices and reminders from your own business address, and see exactly what every client was sent.
public.problem: Your accounting software emails your clients in its own name, on its own schedule, and you cannot always switch those messages off. Long-time clients get chased for invoices they already paid another way, and you find out when they complain. You want every message a client receives to come from you.
public.forWhom: Owners and bookkeepers of small service firms that bill clients through QuickBooks Online.
benefits: Invoices arrive from your own business address
Reminders on your schedule, stopped once a client pays
A clear record of every message each client received

ideas.problemStatement: From August 2026 QuickBooks Online began emailing customers 'Your payment for invoice ... isn't finished yet' after they opened an invoice, with no setting to stop it; owners call it contacting their clients in their name, one filed a BBB complaint, long-time clients who paid by other means threatened to leave, and the workaround is downloading invoices and emailing them by hand. QuickBooks also cannot send from a custom domain or Outlook: only one connected Gmail address.
ideas.description: The firm connects QuickBooks Online and verifies its own domain once. The app pulls each invoice's PDF through the QuickBooks API and sends it, and any reminders, from the firm's domain on the firm's schedule, so the client never needs to receive mail from Intuit. Payment status syncs back from QuickBooks to stop reminders, every message is logged per client and noted on the invoice, and a bookkeeper can run several client companies from one login. Whether sending outside QuickBooks also stops Intuit's own follow-up emails is tested on a live account in milestone 1 before the app claims it.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners and office staff of US solo and small service firms (1 to 20 people) that send roughly 10 to 100 invoices a month from QuickBooks Online, and the bookkeepers who send invoices for them.
ideas.buyer: The owner on the business card, or the outside bookkeeper for several client companies.
ideas.whyNow: Intuit's autumn 2026 rollout of customer-facing 'Finish your payment' emails (98-reply and 20-reply community threads, August to November 2026) broke owners' trust in QuickBooks contacting clients; Intuit is only now trialling a switch on some accounts, and the general wish to send from one's own domain has gone unanswered since at least 2022.
ideas.founderFit: A contained integration (QuickBooks OAuth, PDF fetch, email with domain authentication, schedules) that Pisan can ship alone on the HintWise platform's email and scheduled-job pieces, sold to small service firms, the owner's first-priority buyers.

review.findings: Reviewer re-read thread 375767 (pages 1 and 6; index7 is 404) and 376201 (pages 1 and 2). About 25 distinct non-staff users complained from 2026-08-24 to 2026-11-10; poster G (Nectivo promotion) and poster H (spam link) excluded. Intuit is partly fixing it: poster I saw a new Reminders switch on 2026-11-09 and poster J had it turned off by escalation on 2026-11-10; no Intuit help article on it exists. Poster K (2026-10-10) found disabling payment options did not stop the email, and plain text did not for poster L, so whether sending outside QuickBooks stops it is unproven. Re-scoped away from 'stops Finish your payment emails' to own-domain invoices, reminders and a client log at $19 with no fee; payment link dropped from v1. ideas.summary: For Australian bookkeepers who run payroll for many small Xero employers: one daily view of every client's Payday Super deadline and every returned contribution, sent to the advisor responsible.

public.summary: See every client's super deadline and every returned super payment in one place, each morning.
public.problem: Since July, super must reach the fund within days of each payday, and a payment that bounces has to be fixed fast. But the warning only reaches whoever approved the payment, often your client, and you find out weeks later while preparing their activity statement. Checking each client's file by hand every day is not practical.
public.forWhom: Bookkeepers and payroll advisers in Australia who look after payroll for several small employers.
benefits: Every client's super deadline in one list
Returned payments caught before the deadline passes
Each adviser sees only their own clients
A short morning email instead of opening every file
Fewer surprise penalties for your clients

ideas.problemStatement: Only the person who approves a super payment in Xero hears when it bounces, and it is "not practicable to be constantly refreshing the Super Payments screen ... particularly for Accountants who manage multiple organisations"; under Payday Super the window is short, and practices find "several cases of bounced payments that the clients are not aware of" while preparing BAS. Xero's planned reminder emails go to every payroll admin, which advisers call "pointless".
ideas.description: The practice connects each client's Xero organisation once. A daily job reads posted pay runs and new starters through the Xero Payroll AU API and computes each pay run's Payday Super deadline under the Act, so the practice sees every file's deadlines in one table. Returned contributions enter a register from forwarded fund or clearing-house emails (read by the LLM gateway) or a manual button, each with its re-pay deadline. Each advisor chooses their files and gets a morning email. The Xero API exposes no super batch status, so the app never claims a payment was made; a reconciliation hint shows only when the super payable balance has not cleared by the deadline.
ideas.targetCustomer: Bookkeepers, BAS agents and payroll advisers in Australian practices (1 to 10 staff) who run Xero Payroll with Auto Super for 10 to 60 small employers.

scoreRationale.pain: A 159-vote idea with recent comments (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967118-payroll-expenses/suggestions/51033448-au-payroll-payroll-advisors-to-receive-superannu) and a practice finding bounces clients did not know about (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967118-payroll-expenses/suggestions/51478654-payroll-au-auto-super-in-web-notification-of-bo), with deadlines set by the Act (https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2025A00057/asmade/2025-11-06/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Practices pay AUD 60 to 200 a month for an adjacent cross-client checker (https://apps.xero.com/au/collection/featured-apps/app/bas-ready); no paid job for this task was found.
scoreRationale.reachability: The voters are named practitioners on Xero's board (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967127-practice-tools/suggestions/51176116-au-xero-hq-payroll-manager), but Xero forbids promotion there and listing needs certification (https://developer.xero.com/pricing).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: BAS Ready reads the super-payable signal across clients (https://apps.xero.com/au/collection/featured-apps/app/bas-ready) and Xero has per-organisation reminders planned (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967118-payroll-expenses/suggestions/51085414-au-payroll-payday-super-reminders); left is the per-payday clock and returned register.
scoreRationale.feasibility: The Payroll AU API has no super batch or status endpoint (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI/master/xero-payroll-au.yaml) and Auto Super posts nothing to the ledger until reconciliation (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967118-payroll-expenses/suggestions/51089014-au-payroll-create-an-account-transaction-when-yo); 50 connections on Xero's Core tier.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Employee payloads carry tax file numbers and bank details that must be dropped (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI/master/xero-payroll-au.yaml), plus Xero certification at scale.

review.findings: Reviewer fetched the ideas board (51033448, 51085414, 51478654, 51015442, 51264019, 51861648, 51909208, 51089014), BAS Ready's listing, developer.xero.com/pricing, the Payroll AU spec v20.1.0, the Act, XBert's blog, Wrkr's page and Xero's Xerocon release. Biggest problem: idea 51089014 (17 votes, comments to 2026-10-21) shows approving an Auto Super batch posts nothing to the ledger, so the planned 'inferred unpaid' flag would only measure how far behind bank reconciliation is. BAS Ready already shows super accrued vs payable across clients (AUD 60-200/month); Wrkr shows returns across clients but needs a clearing-house switch; Xero has a per-organisation overview and notifications in development, nothing practice-wide shipped. One complainant wrote both 51861648 and the 51478654 comment and counts once. Return emails reach only the approver. Core tier caps the app at 50 connections and cannot list on the App Store. Employee payloads carry TFNs and bank details. Re-scoped to a Payday Super deadline clock with per-adviser routing and a returned-contribution register; liability check demoted to a labelled hint; member verification left to Wrkr. Total stays 17.

ideas.summary: For small businesses closing, selling or leaving QuickBooks Online: keep a complete, searchable copy of your books for the years the tax office requires, without paying for software you no longer use.

public.summary: Keep a complete, searchable copy of your books after you stop paying for your accounting software.
public.problem: You are closing, selling or switching, but the law says you must keep your records for years. Once you cancel, your accounting software keeps your books readable for a limited time, and after that you pay for a subscription you no longer use just to look something up. The free exports leave out receipts and are hard to search.
public.forWhom: Owners of small businesses leaving their accounting software, and the accountants who look after them.
benefits: Your full history kept for the years required
Receipts stay linked to their transactions
Search any invoice or payment in seconds
Share read-only access with your accountant or a buyer
A reminder before the retention period ends

ideas.problemStatement: Businesses must keep records for years (the IRS says 3 years by default, up to 7 for some claims; Australian advisers cite 7 for the ATO), but QuickBooks Online gives one year of read-only access after cancelling, and Xero users say a restructured client must 'pay for a file he is getting no usage out of' just to view old sales, while a former employee's old payslips 'cannot be downloaded now that the file is in a ledger state'.
ideas.description: Before cancelling, the owner or their accountant connects the QuickBooks Online company once. The app pulls the full history through the API (customers, vendors, invoices, bills, payments, bank transactions, journals and attachments) plus the General Ledger, P&L and balance sheet for each year, verifies counts and totals against QuickBooks, and produces an open-format ZIP that is the record of truth. A hosted read-only viewer lets the owner search any transaction and send expiring read-only links to an accountant, buyer or auditor, and an email reminds them before the retention period ends. Xero follows in a later phase; QuickBooks Desktop is out of scope.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of US small businesses (and their bookkeepers and accountants) that are closing, selling, restructuring or switching away from QuickBooks Online and must keep 3 to 7 years of records.
ideas.buyer: The owner, once per company, or an accounting firm buying a pack for clients who are leaving.
ideas.whyNow: QuickBooks Online and Xero raised US prices in 2026 (Xero from 2026-10-01), pushing small firms to switch or close, and the first done-for-you QuickBooks archive service (Books Backup, $499) launched in October 2026, showing buyers pay for this at the point of cancelling.
ideas.founderFit: An export-and-search build (OAuth, resumable jobs, Postgres full-text search, file storage, share links) that fits the HintWise platform, sold self-serve to small businesses and through accountants; the owner needs no domain credentials to sell it.

problemEvidence.author: Xero user (adviser to small businesses)
problemEvidence.summary: Asks for read-only access to cancelled files: 'We are required to keep data for 7 years ... why can't we have read-only access'; a restructured client pays for a file he gets no use from.

problemEvidence.author: Xero user (commenter on a downgraded file)
problemEvidence.summary: A former employee is asking for old payslips, which 'cannot be downloaded now that the file is in a ledger state'; the idea (opened 2026-05-07) asks for read-only access to reports after downgrading.

problemEvidence.author: Intuit (official help article)
problemEvidence.summary: After cancelling QuickBooks Online, data stays read-only for one year (90 days for trials); Intuit advises exporting or printing data before cancelling.

problemEvidence.author: IRS
problemEvidence.summary: Keep records 3 years by default, 6 if income is under-reported by more than 25%, 7 for bad-debt claims, employment tax records at least 4 years.

problemEvidence.author: Books Backup (vendor)
problemEvidence.summary: Sells a done-for-you QuickBooks Online archive for $499 per company, one-off, delivered in about 5 business days; read on the vendor page.

competitors.name: Books Backup
competitors.gap: Done-for-you through an accountant-user seat and delivered as a static PDF/Excel package; QuickBooks Online only, no hosted search or share links.

competitors.name: Numerint Backup (Xero)
competitors.price: One-off; data-only backup £10, attachments priced per file after a free scan
competitors.gap: Xero only; a ZIP without a hosted viewer, sharing or reminders; no journals, fixed assets or VAT returns.

competitors.name: Control-C (Xero)
competitors.gap: Xero only and a monthly fee for every year of retention (about NZD 1,680 over 7 years).

competitors.name: QuickBooks Online read-only access and exports
competitors.price: Free for one year after cancelling
competitors.gap: Access ends after a year, and the exports do not keep attachments linked to transactions.

keyFeatures: One-click pull of the full QuickBooks Online history
Yearly General Ledger, P&L and balance sheet
Attachments linked to their transactions

Read-only expiring links for accountants and auditors
Open-format ZIP with a verification report
Retention-expiry reminder

features: QuickBooks Online connect and full pull
outOfScope: Restoring data into any accounting system

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind front end; Supabase sign-in, per-app schema with Postgres full-text search and storage for attachments; backend-hub on Render for QuickBooks OAuth and long-running resumable export jobs; scheduled jobs and transactional email for reminders.

pricing.model: One-off fee per company, with hosted access for a stated term
pricing.pricePoint: $149 per company including the ZIP and 7 years of hosted access; accountant pack of 5 for $499
pricing.rationale: Undercuts Books Backup's $499 done-for-you service and seven years of Control-C; the ZIP is the record of truth so hosting is a convenience, not the only copy.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate only: 3 to 8 archives a month in year one through bookkeepers x $149 = about $5,000 to $14,000 a year; one accounting-firm partnership could double it.
ideas.distribution: The QuickBooks community bans pitching and 'we do not allow people to post links to external content of any kind' (guidelines post), and the buyer is reachable only around the moment of cancelling. First 10: bookkeepers and ProAdvisors with clients who are closing, selling or switching (the accountant pack), plus a search page for 'cancel QuickBooks keep records'.

validationTest.method: Landing page and outreach to about 30 bookkeepers and ProAdvisors, offering free archives to the first 5 clients who are closing or switching.
validationTest.successCriteria: 5 completed archives and 2 paid pre-orders at $149 within 3 weeks.

ideas.moat: Weak: accountant relationships and, later, coverage of both QuickBooks Online and Xero with one hosted viewer.
compliance: Holds years of financial records and personal data (customers, vendors, possibly employees): encryption, least-privilege scopes, privacy notice, deletion on request.
Long-term custody: a written shutdown and export guarantee, with the open ZIP as the customer's own copy.
Intuit production keys need its app assessment; metered API reads.
IRS electronic records must remain accurate and accessible; the app must not claim to be an official archive.

risks.risk: Books Backup, Numerint and Control-C already serve most of the job.
risks.mitigation: Compete on self-serve price, hosted search and share links, and sell through accountants.

risks.risk: Seven-year custody by a one-person business.
risks.mitigation: Make the downloadable ZIP the deliverable, host as a convenience, and publish a shutdown policy.

risks.risk: API limits and attachment volume make large companies slow to export.
risks.mitigation: Resumable jobs over several days, started well inside the one-year read-only window.

scoreRationale.pain: Dated complaints exist (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967121-users-setup/suggestions/51858312-view-data-when-file-cancelled, https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967133-reports-tax/suggestions/51272953-reporting-include-read-only-access-to-all-reports) but with 1 to 2 votes, and QuickBooks Online gives a free year of read-only access (https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/access-permissions/happens-quickbooks-online-data-cancel/L6qDpbE1B_US_en_US).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Buyers pay $499 one-off for a done-for-you archive (https://booksbackup.com/) and use paid Xero backups (https://apps.xero.com/uk/app/numerintbackup).
scoreRationale.reachability: Buyers appear only around cancellation and the QuickBooks community bans links; the incumbent sells through accountants (https://booksbackup.com/), which is the realistic route.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Books Backup (https://booksbackup.com/), Numerint and Control-C (https://apps.xero.com/nz/app/controlc) cover most of the job; the gap is a cheap self-serve hosted archive with sharing.
scoreRationale.feasibility: QuickBooks attachments and reports are available through the API but production approval, metered reads and long exports make it multi-week; Xero's Journals endpoint needs its top API tier (https://developer.xero.com/pricing).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Seven years of custody of financial and personal data by one person (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records).

review.findings: Reviewer re-read the QuickBooks Desktop view-only thread (93519): all posts are about Desktop licences, with free workarounds (Enterprise trial, clock rollback), so they do not support a QuickBooks Online or Xero archive and are not counted; the Desktop import was dropped. Xero ideas 51858312 (1 vote) and 51272953 (2 votes) are real but thin, and Xero staff say reports can be published before downgrading. The Freelancer job (2026-09-18, $10-30) is a move to spreadsheets, not an archive, and is not counted. Books Backup ($499, QuickBooks Online, done-for-you), Numerint (Xero, £10 data-only) and Control-C (NZD 19.99/month) cover most of the job; nothing free covers 5 to 7 years with attachments. Xero's Journals endpoint is on the Advanced tier (AUD 1,445/month), so Xero moves to phase 2. Seven-year custody is a real liability; the ZIP becomes the record of truth. Re-scoped to QuickBooks Online only, self-serve, $149. Scores cut to pain 3, reachability 2, competitiveGap 2, feasibility 2, complianceBurden 2. Total 16 (research) to 14.

runNotes.caveats: First run of 2026-11-19 (Thursday, small business back-office lens). No candidate came near the gate of 22: 23 candidates were generated (20 new from three gatherers and the coordinator, plus 3 re-researched watchlist entries). Eight were researched; the Toggl invoicing idea died in research (Toggl's own API spec documents a native invoicing beta) and two more fell below the watchlist line in research (Square front-desk brief, Jobber work-order inbox). Five ideas were adversarially reviewed: four survived, all rescored (lesson series booker 20 to 19, own-domain invoice mail 17 to 18, Payday Super clock 17 to 17 with a re-scope, books archive 16 to 14) and one was killed (Stripe exceptions for Invoice Ninja). Every shipped idea is provisional. Selection constraint not met: no shipped idea is a Weekend MVP; the only Weekend MVP candidate that reached review (Stripe exceptions for Invoice Ninja) was killed. Order of review: the books archive (research total 16) was reviewed before unresearched candidates with higher preliminary totals (the BC time-zone audit at 21, the Calendly text-consent tracker, the Peppol explainer and the year-end pack at 20), and the Payday Super clock (17) after them; reviewing stopped at five with four survivors; those four unresearched candidates go to the watchlist for re-research. The books archive evidence excludes a long QuickBooks Desktop lockout thread, which the reviewer judged off-target for a QuickBooks Online archive. The Payday Super rule is 7 business days after payday (20 for new employees) per the Act on legislation.gov.au; ato.gov.au and fairwork.gov.au could not be read. Authors who post under a full real name are recorded by role.
